patch.value: Linked-test commands are merge-unioned workspace data executed with shell:true — no provenance, allowlist, or confirmation boundary

Linked test commands are arbitrary shell strings stored in item data and executed without any trust boundary. src/sdk/test/execution.ts createLinkedTestChild spawns the stored command with shell:true, cwd process.cwd(), detached on POSIX, inheriting the caller's environment; there is no allowlist, no confirmation prompt, no dry-run default, and no provenance check anywhere in that path or in src/cli/commands/test.ts. The exposure is created by the merge model this project deliberately adopted: docs/MERGE_SAFETY.md specifies that append-like item collections merge by set union, so a linked test added on another branch is silently unioned into the item on merge, and the merge drivers are installed repo-wide by pm merge install. A maintainer or agent who then runs 'pm test <id> --run' or 'pm test-all' executes whatever command arrived with that merge. Every documented multi-agent workflow in this repo — fleet lanes, worktree agents, branch merges — routes through exactly that sequence. Duplicate check: searched linked test/shell/untrusted/trust boundary all-status. pm-g072 (closed) hardened untrusted dependency specs reaching npm install during extension install, a different input path; pm-pim7 owns secret guarding; pm-u14c owns author authenticity and pm-xc68 policy roles, both about who wrote a mutation rather than what executing stored data is allowed to do; pm-3z0k owns detached attestation. No item owns execution trust for linked test commands.

A documented trust boundary governs linked-test execution: pm records provenance for every linked test command (author, source branch or merge origin, and whether it arrived through a merge rather than a local mutation); executing a command whose provenance is not locally trusted requires an explicit opt-in (config policy plus an explicit flag) instead of running silently; pm validate or pm health surfaces linked test commands that changed through a merge since the last local acknowledgment; docs/TESTING.md and docs/MERGE_SAFETY.md state the boundary and the threat model explicitly; the default behaviour for a workspace whose items were only mutated locally is unchanged so no existing workflow regresses; regression tests cover merge-introduced commands, the opt-in path, and the refusal path
Make stored-then-executed workspace data safe under the multi-agent merge model pm is designed for

pm's core promise is that many agents merge tracker state across branches without conflict; execution of merged data must not be a silent code-execution path, or the merge model becomes the attack surface

The merge-safety wave shipped and pm merge install is now standard bootstrap; pm-76dnfg is building randomized N-branch merge conformance, which is exactly the point to state what merged execution data is allowed to do
src/sdk/test/execution.ts createLinkedTestChild; docs/MERGE_SAFETY.md set-union semantics for append-like collections; .gitattributes pm-item-toon/pm-item-markdown drivers

Branch A adds a linked test to an item via pm test <id> --add; merge branch A into branch B where the pm merge drivers are installed; the command is unioned into the item on B; running pm test <id> --run on B executes it with shell:true and the caller's environment
A linked test command that arrived from another branch cannot execute silently; pm makes its provenance visible and requires explicit acknowledgment before running it
pm test --run and pm test-all spawn any stored command string with shell:true, with no provenance, allowlist, confirmation, or post-merge advisory

value.text: Code evidence: src/sdk/test/execution.ts createLinkedTestChild calls spawn(command, { cwd: process.cwd(), env, shell: true, windowsHide: true, detached: process.platform !== 'win32' }). A grep for allowlist, allowList, confirm, --yes, trusted or sanitiz across src/sdk/test/execution.ts and src/cli/commands/test.ts returns nothing, so no guard exists on that path. docs/TESTING.md mentions shell syntax only as an authoring convenience and docs/MERGE_SAFETY.md documents that append-like item collections merge by set union — which is the mechanism that lets a linked test authored on one branch appear on another without a local mutation. The repo's own bootstrap instructs every clone to run 'pm merge install', so the union semantics are active by default in exactly the multi-agent branch workflows this project targets.
